name: Keturah Tuttle

residences.note: Her husband Thomas Lamoureux and probable brothers James Tuttle and John Tuthill all signed the 1775 Articles of Association in Cornwall Precinct

bioAdditions:
No record found this round names Keturah's parents directly, so her parentage stays probable. New circumstantial support: the 1775 Cornwall Precinct association list carries both 'James Tuttle' and 'John Tuthill' as well as her husband Thomas Lamoureux (S3). On Alva Tuttle's reconstruction these are her twin brothers James and John (b. 1753). Her mother Temperance Smith's place in the family of James Smith & Jerusha Topping is now backed by two independent printed authorities: Pelletreau (1898) and C. H. Weygant's Family Record (1897), which names James and Jerusha's daughters Eunice, Keturah, Temperance and Jerusha and puts Capt. Austin and Capt. Francis Smith, their sons, at Woodbury Clove 'some twenty years or more' before the Revolution (S1, S2). Keturah was evidently named for her aunt Keturah Smith.

The printed list of pre-1784 New York marriage licenses has no Lamoreaux-Tuthill (or Tuthill-Smith) entry, so these marriages were probably by banns (S4).

relationships.evidence: Temperance appears among the daughters of James Smith & Jerusha Topping in two independent compiled sources (Pelletreau 1898; Weygant 1897). Keturah's own children bear the names Temperance and Keturah, and her husband served under Temperance's brother Capt. Francis Smith.

openQuestionsNew: Is there a Cornwall/Monroe church record (e.g. Bethlehem Presbyterian) of Keturah's marriage to Thomas Lamoreaux, c. 1772?
